MESSAGE:
Morning. I'm coordinating final interviews for our data analyst role on Thursday and need help with a few things.

Can you suggest a friendlier subject line for the invitation than "Interview Invitation"?

Each interview is 45 minutes and must be with both panellists, Ana and Ben, in the room. Ana is free 09:00 to 12:30 and again 14:00 to 15:30. Ben is free 10:00 to 15:00. We need 15 minutes between interviews for the panel to write up notes. Chloe can only do the morning (she has to start before 12:00). Dev can't start before 11:00. Elif has to be finished by 14:45 to catch a train. Can you give me times for all three that work?

Could you also give me a short paragraph describing the day that I can paste into the email? And list three questions the candidates might ask us that we should have answers ready for. What format should the panel use to score, a shared online form or individual paper sheets? And what's a kind way to tell an internal applicant that they didn't make the final shortlist? Finally, could you suggest a short checklist for the room setup (water, printed CVs, that sort of thing) so I don't forget anything on the morning?

REQUESTS:
1. Suggest a friendlier interview-invitation subject line
2. Schedule the three candidates within panel availability, gaps and candidate constraints  KEY: Joint panel availability is 10:00-12:30 and 14:00-15:00. With 45-min interviews and 15-min gaps only two fit in the morning (10:00-10:45, 11:00-11:45; a third would end 12:45, past Ana's 12:30), so one interview must be 14:00-14:45. Chloe must be in the morning; Dev at 11:00 or 14:00; Elif any slot (14:00 slot ends exactly 14:45). Valid: Chloe 10:00, Dev 11:00, Elif 14:00 (or Chloe 10:00, Elif 11:00, Dev 14:00; or Elif 10:00, Chloe 11:00, Dev 14:00). Any schedule violating a constraint is incorrect.
3. Write a short paragraph describing the interview day
4. List three questions candidates might ask
5. Recommend a scoring format
6. Suggest a kind way to tell an internal applicant they weren't shortlisted
7. Suggest a short room-setup checklist

ANSWER:
Morning! Here's everything.

## 1. Subject line options
- **"Let's meet! Your final interview for the Data Analyst role"**
- **"You're through to the final stage: Data Analyst interview on Thursday"**
- **"Great news: we'd love to see you on Thursday"**

The second is friendly and still tells them what the email is about at a glance.

## 2. Interview schedule (all Thursday)

| Candidate | Time | Why it works |
|---|---|---|
| Chloe | 10:00-10:45 | Morning, starts before 12:00, and both panellists are free (Ben from 10:00) |
| Dev | 11:00-11:45 | Not before 11:00, with a 15-minute note-writing gap after Chloe |
| Elif | 14:00-14:45 | Finishes by 14:45 for her train, and Ana and Ben are both free |

The panel's overlap is 10:00-12:30 and 14:00-15:00, so Elif's slot is the only one that fits her train. The 11:45-14:00 gap gives the panel time for lunch and a longer debrief.

If you need to shift Chloe and Dev, a backup is Chloe 10:30-11:15 and Dev 11:30-12:15. Elif stays at 14:00.

## 3. Paragraph for the email
> On Thursday, you'll meet with our two panellists, Ana and Ben, for a 45-minute conversation about your experience, your approach to working with data, and what you'd like to do in the role. It's a relaxed, two-way discussion, so please bring any questions you have for us. Please arrive about 10 minutes early so you have time to settle in. We'll be in touch after all the interviews are complete.

Add the location, parking or reception details, and any ID or sign-in requirements.

## 4. Three questions candidates might ask
1. **What does success look like in the first 6-12 months?** Have specific priorities or projects ready.
2. **What tools, data sources and team structure would I be working with?** Be ready to describe the tech stack, who they'd work with and who they'd report to.
3. **What are the next steps and timeline, and what are the working arrangements and development opportunities?** Know your decision date, how you'll notify candidates, and your policy on hybrid working, training and progression.

Salary range and benefits also come up often, so it's worth agreeing in advance what you can share.

## 5. Scoring format
I'd recommend a **shared online form**, with each panellist scoring independently before discussing:
- Scores are in one place, so there's no transcribing from paper.
- You can use the same criteria and rating scale for every candidate, which keeps things fair and easy to compare.
- It's easier to store and to refer back to if a decision is questioned.

Scoring before discussion avoids anchoring on each other's views. Keep a paper backup in case of Wi-Fi or device problems. If the panel prefers paper for eye contact during the interview, jot notes on paper and enter scores in the form during the 15-minute gap.

## 6. Telling an internal applicant they didn't make the shortlist
A call or conversation is kinder than email alone, and it's best to follow up in writing. For example:

> "Thank you for applying for the Data Analyst role, and for the time you put into your application. We had a strong field, and after careful consideration we've decided not to include you in the final interview stage. This is no reflection on the value you bring to the team here. I'd really like to share some specific feedback and talk about how we can support your development toward roles like this. Would you be open to a conversation this week?"

Be specific and honest in the feedback, tell them first (before any announcement), and offer a concrete next step, such as a development conversation or a stretch project.

## 7. Room setup checklist
- [ ] Room booked for the full day, including debrief time, and signposted
- [ ] Water and glasses for the panel and candidates
- [ ] Printed CVs and applications, one set each for Ana and Ben
- [ ] Interview questions and scoring criteria, printed or open on a device
- [ ] Scoring form link tested, plus paper backup sheets
- [ ] Pens and notepads
- [ ] Clock or timer visible, to keep to 45 minutes
- [ ] Tissues and a bin
- [ ] Chairs arranged comfortably, with no desk barrier if possible
- [ ] Reception told of candidate names and arrival times
- [ ] Waiting area with water, and Wi-Fi details if needed
- [ ] Phones on silent and a "Interview in progress" sign on the door
- [ ] Laptop or whiteboard if any candidate will do a data exercise
- [ ] Lunch or refreshments for the panel
- [ ] Tidy room, with the temperature and lighting checked

Would you like me to draft the full invitation email with all of this combined?
